clue.text: Got up to make deliveries, which may be under arrangement?

blocks.note: past tense of rise: got up out of bed
in cricket a bowler delivers the ball, so to bowl is to make deliveries

explanation.surface: Someone rises early to do a delivery round, wondering what might be arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests post or milk, but in cricket each ball sent down is a delivery. The definition is cryptic: a flower arrangement sits on top of this vase.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bowl is a round vase holding cut flowers, so it sits underneath a floral display.

clue.text: Does twist? Bolero often follows this

blocks.note: first meaning: tangles or entwines, a present-tense verb
second meaning: the composer's possessive, as in the famous orchestral piece's full title

explanation.walkthrough: Read as RAVEL'S, the second half is the composer Maurice Ravel: 'Ravel's Bolero' is how the piece is usually named, so his name comes just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to tangle threads together, and Bolero is the best-known orchestral work by the French composer Maurice Ravel.

clue.text: One who’s drafted isn’t taking against longhand

indicators.note: declining to take something means leaving it out, so a part is removed

blocks.note: a conscript is someone drafted into military service
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A draftee objects to writing things out by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drafted' hints at writing a draft, but it means called up for military service. Removing CON from CONSCRIPT leaves SCRIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Script is handwriting, especially joined-up writing, which is what longhand means as opposed to shorthand or typing.

clue.text: Listen carefully to sounds of brooks around middle of glen

indicators.note: the middle is the central part, so only the inner letters of a word are kept
going around something encloses it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: to brook is to tolerate or bear
a glen is a VALLEY; its middle four letters

explanation.surface: A walker listens to the babbling streams running through a Scottish valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brooks' looks like streams, but here it is the verb: to brook is to put up with. A glen is a Scottish valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all ears is an idiom for paying complete attention, giving your whole hearing to what is being said.

clue.text: One staying behind in person?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who remains behind personally rather than leaving
setter's reading: the cricket fielder who stands behind the stumps all innings, never bowling or batting while fielding

explanation.surface: Someone who stays back after everyone else has gone, in the flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket one fielder crouches directly behind the batter's stumps throughout; 'in person' plays on the gloves-on, always-present role of that player.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder in cricket who wears gloves and stands behind the stumps to catch balls the batter misses.

clue.text: Boot’s fit needing nine regularly

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: fit and healthy: well
second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A boot that only fits properly if it is size nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' reads as the fit of a shoe, but it means healthy. A wellie is a British rubber boot for wet weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for wellington, the waterproof rubber boot worn in mud and rain, so it is one kind of footwear.

clue.text: Perhaps meet five out of seventeen

indicators.note: taken out of a longer word, so a run of consecutive letters is lifted from it

blocks.note: tells how many letters to lift
five consecutive letters inside this number

explanation.surface: Picking five items from a set of seventeen, perhaps at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Five' is the count of letters taken, not a number to use: s(EVENT)een. 'Perhaps' warns that a meet is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A meet, such as an athletics meeting, is one example of an organised sporting occasion.

clue.text: Call which people hope to make with letters?

definitions.text: which people hope to make with letters?

blocks.note: first meaning: the military bugle call played at the end of the day and at funerals

blocks.clueFragment: which people hope to make with letters?
blocks.note: second meaning: the final mail collection of the day, which you try to catch

explanation.walkthrough: The bugle call is the British name for the evening call also sounded at remembrance services; the second reading is catching the final collection from a postbox.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a military bugle signal and the final daily collection of mail from a British postbox.

clue.text: Worry king’s trapped by duty

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: Edward Rex, the royal cipher
excise is a tax or duty on goods

explanation.surface: A king is anxious about being caught by his obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty' looks like obligation, but it is a tax. ER stands for Edward Rex (King Edward) as well as the more familiar Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise someone is to trouble or preoccupy them, as in being exercised about an issue.

clue.text: Disagreement heretic enters into versus church

indicators.note: entering a space means going inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation
a follower of Arius, an early Christian heretic
Church of England

explanation.surface: A heretic's arrival sparks a dispute set against the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The heretic goes between V and CE. Arians denied the full divinity of Christ, and the name is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at variance with someone is to be in conflict with them, so the noun names a dispute.

clue.text: Tenant without cover for expense

indicators.note: a cover wraps the outside, so only the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: less means minus or without
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A renter without insurance cover for costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests insurance, but it means the letters on the outside of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds property under a lease, which makes them the renter paying the landlord.

clue.text: Magnetic problem with recording north upright up the pole

indicators.note: British slang for crazy or confused, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A compass needle stands straight up at the North Pole, a magnetic puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magnetic', 'north' and 'pole' all push towards compasses; the magnetism is actually in recording tape, and 'up the pole' means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: On magnetic tape, signal from one wound layer can transfer onto the next, producing faint echoes: a known defect in analogue recording.

clue.text: Feature of jacket has lines cut by someone clumsy

indicators.note: something cut is split open, and the thing doing the cutting ends up inside

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for plural
an ape is a clumsy, oafish person

explanation.surface: A tailor's jacket has seams badly cut by a ham-fisted worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Ls are split apart by the clumsy one.
explanation.definitionFit: The folded-back flap on the front of a jacket or coat, below the collar.

clue.text: Able to live in many places using EU railway to choose mostly

definitions.text: Able to live in many places

indicators.note: most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
RY is an abbreviation for railway
taken as written
to choose is to pick

explanation.surface: Using European rail to pick where you live lets you settle almost anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: A rare scientific word built plainly from its parts; PICK loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In ecology a eurytopic species tolerates a wide range of habitats, the opposite of a specialist confined to one.

clue.text: Crates preparing to take off with other holidaymakers?

definitions.text: preparing to take off with other holidaymakers?

blocks.note: first meaning: wooden boxes for transporting goods

blocks.clueFragment: preparing to take off with other holidaymakers?
blocks.note: second meaning: filling suitcases before a flight, read as a verb phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: travellers getting ready for a trip are packing their cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Packing cases are large boxes for shipping goods, and people about to fly off are literally packing suitcases.

clue.text: Church musician upset his rector

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A church singer has annoyed the parish priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as the musician offending the rector, but it tells you to rearrange the two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a singer in a church choir, one kind of musician serving in worship.

clue.text: Counters scuba failing amid rising waters

indicators.note: something failing is breaking down, so its letters fall into a new order
amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside another
in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
the sea is a body of water

explanation.surface: Scuba gear breaks down as the tide comes in, a diver's nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counters' looks like a verb, but it is a plural noun; the jumbled diving word sits inside the upturned water.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used for calculating, so these devices are things for reckoning numbers.

clue.text: Pumice, perhaps light, which forms moving blobs

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the thing that does this, not a noun

blocks.note: pumice is a type of solidified volcanic rock
a lamp is a light

explanation.surface: Pumice stone is light and forms lumps that float and drift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' seems to describe how little pumice weighs; it is a noun for a lamp. 'Perhaps' marks pumice as one example of the rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A lava lamp is a decorative 1960s light in which heated wax rises and falls in coloured liquid.

clue.text: Is bass cornet playing in this?

definitions.note: the whole clue points to it: the part of an orchestra containing these instruments

indicators.note: playing with something means moving it around freely, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bass cornet is being played in some part of the band?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' is literal in the surface and the anagram signal in the wordplay; 'this' asks which group the cornet belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornet is a brass instrument, so it plays in the orchestra or band group made up of trumpets, horns and tubas.

clue.text: Took food back to consume best

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: past tense of feed
to consume food is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone returned the food so they could eat the finest dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' reads as an adjective for the finest, but it is a verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best an opponent is to beat or overcome them, the same action as winning against them.

clue.text: Recycled rubbish female has left daughter

indicators.note: someone who has left is gone, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: refuse is household waste
the usual abbreviation
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A woman recycled the rubbish and then her daughter moved out.
explanation.walkthrough: REFUSE loses F and gains D at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Recycled material has been put to use again instead of being thrown out as waste.

clue.text: After noise of display very loudly regret backing driver

indicators.note: a noise is what reaches the ear, so the word is chosen by its sound
coming after means following on, so the later pieces are placed behind the first
backing means moving backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a display is a show; CHAU is spelt the French way but said the same
fortissimo in music notation
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: After a loud show-off moment, someone bitterly regrets reversing the car.
explanation.walkthrough: The first syllable of the answer is pronounced like 'show', which is what the display gives. FF is the musical marking for very loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeur is a person employed to drive a private car, so the word is a specific kind of driver.

clue.text: Peel off fine red pigment

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
lake is a crimson pigment used by painters

explanation.surface: A fine coat of red paint is starting to come away.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake here is not water but an artist's crimson dye, a sense solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: When paint flakes it comes away in thin pieces, which is what peeling off describes.

clue.text: Girl’s wrath and anger oddly vanishing

indicators.note: the odd-numbered positions disappear, so only even letters remain

blocks.note: ire is anger or wrath
second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A girl's fury and rage gradually fade away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anger' tempts as a second synonym for fury, but its letters are thinned out instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female given name, and crosswords use girl to clue any woman's first name.

clue.text: Medicine man using fake article

blocks.note: a sham is a fake
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A healer who relies on a counterfeit object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like an item, but it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a spiritual healer in traditional societies, the figure often called a witch doctor or medicine man.

clue.text: Lock by only pier

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: A canal lock located beside a lone jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' and 'pier' suggest waterways, but the lock is hair and the pier is part of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture a pier is a solid supporting column or mass of masonry, like a projecting support against a wall.

clue.text: Higher following small meal

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the pieces sit one behind the other

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
upper means higher

explanation.surface: A larger portion after a small snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small meal' looks like the definition, but 'small' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal, often a light one eaten late in the day.

clue.text: During interval half of cast, note, needed a drink

indicators.note: only half survives, so the rest of the word is cut away
during means in the course of, so a piece falls inside another

blocks.note: in music a third is an interval between notes
its second half
a musical note

explanation.surface: During the theatre interval half the cast needed a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interval' suggests the break at the theatre, but it is the musical gap called a third.
explanation.definitionFit: To thirst is to crave liquid, so having thirsted means you were in need of something to drink.
